articles.headline: What's next for Jayden Daniels, Commanders after elbow injury?
articles.description: Experts weigh in on Daniels' latest injury and what it means for him, the Commanders and their collective futures.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- For nearly an entire half on Sunday, Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels resembled the player from 2024, the one who was named NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year and mentioned as a future league MVP.

On the final drive of the first half at the Dallas Cowboys, Daniels provided reminders of that season: He ran for 24 yards and threw for another 27, including a strike on third-and-6 to Stefon Diggs for 10 yards.

Then, on the final play of the half, the 2025 version of Daniels showed up, the one who missed 10 games with three different injuries. He suffered a dislocated left elbow, leaving the Commanders with plenty of questions about the future -- from his durability to whether they had built a good enough roster to withstand his absence for even a short period.

Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Daniels will visit specialists Tuesday and Wednesday to determine the best course of action. It's the same injury Daniels sustained in Week 9 last season; he returned in Week 14, but after reinjuring the elbow in that contest, the Commanders shut him down for the final four games of the campaign.

His latest injury has left Washington in a familiar spot: wondering what this means for Daniels' future and trying to piece together wins. Last season, the Commanders struggled to do the latter and finished 5-12. Washington is 0-2 now and will face the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in its home opener Sunday.

"0-2 is not where we wanted to be, that's for sure," Quinn said. "But we also are resolute that that's not where we're going to be staying."

Commanders reporter John Keim and senior fantasy writer Eric Karabell weigh in on Daniels' latest injury and what it means for him, the Commanders and their collective futures.

Is the season lost?

It's only two games. But after last season, when injuries -- notably the one to Daniels -- derailed the Commanders, it would require a leap of faith to think otherwise at this point, particularly in the NFC East. Even if Daniels had remained healthy, Washington is now 0-2 in the division. So, the road would have been tough regardless. Also, the Commanders will next face Seattle in their home opener and in the coming six weeks will play the Giants twice, the 49ers, the Rams and the Eagles.

If Daniels is out multiple weeks, that's a steep task. And this isn't about backup quarterback Marcus Mariota, who will start Sunday, as much as it is about what the Commanders haven't shown in other areas.

The sad aspect for Washington is that Daniels was playing well. He was sharp and showed the dynamic ability that made him the No. 2 pick in the 2024 draft, and a player multiple high-profile coaches liked best in that class.

"I loved everything about the first half, how he was playing," Quinn said of Sunday's performance, as Daniels rushed for 69 yards and threw for 96 yards and a touchdown before the injury.

But Daniels also covers up a lot of flaws. Those flaws will now be magnified,

articles.headline: Chargers placing TEs David Njoku, Charlie Kolar on IR
articles.description: The Chargers are placing tight ends David Njoku and Charlie Kolar on injured reserve, coach Jim Harbaugh announced Monday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are placing tight ends David Njoku and Charlie Kolar on injured reserve, coach Jim Harbaugh announced Monday.

The moves, which will sideline both players for at least four games, will leave the Chargers with one tight end -- Oronde Gadsden -- on the active roster.

Njoku was carted off the field in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders with a fibula injury. Kolar has a forearm injury.

Kolar will be out "about a month," a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Njoku appeared to get injured while blocking for running back Omarion Hampton. The entire team came out onto the field to give Njoku well wishes as he exited.

The Chargers signed Njoku to a one-year deal in May after he spent his first nine seasons with the Cleveland Browns. Kolar signed a three-year, $24.3 million contract with the Chargers in March after he spent his first four seasons with the Baltimore Ravens.

Njoku has eight receptions for 67 yards this season, while Kolar has three receptions for 21 yards.

The Chargers are 0-2 to start the season after upset losses at home to the Arizona Cardinals and Raiders. Coming into this season, ESPN's Football Power Index gave the Chargers the fifth-highest chance to win the Super Bowl.

ESPN's Kris Rhim contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Sources: Eagles TE Dallas Goedert has MCL sprain
articles.description: Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert is likely to miss a few weeks due to a sprained MCL, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert is likely to miss a few weeks due to a sprained MCL he suffered in Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Goedert was targeted twice and had one catch for 4 yards before leaving the game with the injury in the second quarter.

He is coming off his best season in 2025 when he reached career highs of 60 receptions and 11 touchdowns.

Goedert, 31, is in his ninth season with the Eagles after being chosen in the second round of the 2018 draft. A durable presence in Philadelphia, Goedert has played in at least 10 games every year.

articles.headline: Sources: Colts WR Alec Pierce seeking second opinion on heel
articles.description: Colts WR Alec Pierce is seeking a second opinion on his left heel injury, sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce is seeking a second opinion on the left heel injury that knocked him out of Sunday night's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday.

Pierce is considered week-to-week, a source said. 

The injury is to the same heel that Pierce had surgically repaired in March. X-rays after the game were negative and head coach Shane Steichen said Monday the Colts are "still gathering information."

 

Pierce, the Colts' top wideout, was unable to put any weight on his left leg and needed assistance exiting the game with 1:45 left in the first quarter. After an initial exam in the medical tent, Pierce was carted to the locker room for X-rays. 

Pierce, who signed a four-year, $114 million contract in March, was expected to be a centerpiece of the Colts' offense this season. But recovery from the procedure on his heel spilled into training camp and lingered past the preseason. He finally returned to practice late last month and was expecting to ramp up his playing time in the weeks to come after being cleared to play in Week 1.

With Pierce out, veteran receiver Laquon Treadwell took the majority of his snaps against the Chiefs and finished with three catches for 61 yards.

ESPN's Stephen Holder contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Sources: Cubs' Bregman suffered facial fractures from foul ball
articles.description: Chicago Cubs star Alex Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures after being struck by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle Sunday, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
articles.body:
Chicago Cubs star Alex Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures after being struck by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle Sunday, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.

Bregman will not undergo surgery and is hopeful to return in the postseason.

In the fourth inning of the Cubs' 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds, left-handed batting Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Reds right-hander Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immediately jogged toward the Cubs' dugout with a hand covering the left side of his face.

Bregman was escorted by an athletic trainer down the dugout steps and into the clubhouse, with blood visible on his face.

Bregman was hospitalized in the Cincinnati area to undergo tests, but posted on Instagram earlier Monday that he was back in Chicago.

"He got hit in the left cheekbone essentially, under the eye," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said after the game. "He was bleeding from his nose a little. There's some swelling. It's a terrible, terrible accident. We hope he's OK."

articles.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Dalton Schultz, Jonah Coleman highlight top options for Week 3
articles.description: Eric Karabell lists who he thinks are the top available players worth adding for the week ahead.
articles.body:
Each Monday, before the current NFL week ends, we will identify players worthy of your attention available in at least 50% of ESPN standard leagues. Things change quickly for player valuation and roles each week in the NFL, and free agency is a critical way to acquire players. We are here to help!

Top pickup options at every position

Looking for the top recommendation at each skill position? Look no further! Here are the players to target heading into Week 3, along with their current roster percentages and a recommendation of how much of your free agent budget (FAB) you should consider using for your bid. 

Tyler Shough, QB, Saints (rostered in 49.7% of leagues, 10-15% of your FAB)

Last week's most recommended QB remains available in barely more than half of ESPN's standard leagues, though likely not for long after yet another solid performance (22.38 points) in a road win against the mighty Baltimore Ravens. This week, the New Orleans Saints host the unbeaten Las Vegas Raiders. Ignore the records. It's a positive matchup. Shough looks like more than a streamer, too, especially since the NFC South doesn't exactly feature top defensive teams and the Saints haven't played any division games yet.

Jonah Coleman, RB, Broncos (15.2% rostered, 10-12% FAB)

Starter J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) wasn't doing so much when he left the game in the second half, having scored just 3.6 points, and rookie Coleman helped spark the offense with his 14.8 points, including a touchdown run. Coleman, a fourth-round pick from Washington, barely played in Week 1, but now he might be his team's starter for this week against the Los Angeles Rams -- pending the status of Dobbins and RJ Harvey (also a hamstring issue) -- and perhaps beyond.

 Denzel Boston, WR, Browns (26.4%, 8-10% FAB):

The rookie Boston scored a touchdown in a blowout Week 1 loss. It was nice, but not really a reason to trust him in Week 2. Then he scored another TD on Sunday. Now, he is quite intriguing, even considering Cleveland's QB situation. Boston is averaging 22 yards per reception through two games. If you wish to invest in a Browns receiver, Boston is the top option over fellow rookie KC Concepcion (57.6%) and the quite invisible Jerry Jeudy (22.1%).

Dalton Schultz, TE, Texans (21.3%, 2% FAB):

Schultz was the main (and perhaps only) beneficiary of the Nico Collins (hamstring) injury, catching 12 passes for 140 yards and achieving 26 fantasy points. No other member of the Houston Texans reached six catches or 40 receiving yards. We really shouldn't be so surprised, though. Schultz ended last season with 82 receptions -- tied for third among tight ends -- and 10th at the position in fantasy points. He might lack the upside of other top tight ends, but his is a relatively high floor, whether Collins plays or not.

articles.headline: Hawks rookie Henri Veesaar (ACL) expected to miss season
articles.description: Hawks rookie 7-footer Henri Veesaar suffered a torn ACL in his right knee during a workout last week and is expected to miss the season.
articles.body:
Atlanta Hawks rookie center Henri Veesaar is expected to miss the 2026-27 season after tearing the ACL in his right knee.

Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15 and will undergo surgery in October. The 7-foot center was drafted with the 52nd overall pick by the LA Clippers and was traded to Atlanta.

Veesaar, 22, averaged 17 points, 8.7 rebounds, 1.2 blocks and 42.6% 3-point shooting in 31 starts for North Carolina during his senior season.

The Hawks also announced they signed guard Isaac McKneely, who averaged 6.7 points, 1.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 18.9 minutes during Atlanta's two summer leagues.
